properties.statement: [BL-156] "Export exactly once per COMMIT" is insufficient under the squash-merge the same document mandates, and it broke the chain on main
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-01 by the gate, immediately after merging PR #21 \u2014 the first PR in this project's history to carry two exporting commits.* AGENTS.md said \"Export the design EXACTLY ONCE per commit, straight onto the committed file\", and that rule was followed exactly. It is still not enough. PRs merge by SQUASH, so N commits become one on main, and only the LAST export's prev_content_hash survives. PR #21 had three commits: a COORD claim (no export), BL-149..152 (export, linking correctly to v0.21.0's 799b06d9), and BL-153..155 (export, linking to the *branch* intermediate da60a633). The squash kept the second export's link \u2014 pointing at a document main never saw. main's chain now reads cd6e6c8: 799b06d9 \u2192 56bc698: prev da60a633, and the gate caught it on the very next run with the right message. WHY IT HAD NEVER FIRED BEFORE, and this is the uncomfortable part: PRs #18 and #19 ALSO carried two commits each and were fine \u2014 because their first commit was the COORD claim, which touches no export. They complied by accident, not by rule. The rule as written has been insufficient for every multi-commit PR this project has ever merged; it simply had not yet met one where two commits both exported. THIS IS THE req:schema-prose-is-checked FAMILY AGAIN, in the process layer \u2014 a written instruction that is correct as stated and wrong in the workflow it is embedded in, exactly like [BL-114]'s finding prose and [BL-152]'s skill prose. Three surfaces now: schema, findings, skills, and process. FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE: AGENTS.md now says once per PULL REQUEST, explains the squash mechanism, and states the corollary that the claim commit goes first. THE CHAIN IS REPAIRED FORWARD, NOT BACKWARD: re-exporting onto the committed file makes every future link sound, but the hole at 56bc698 is history and stays on the record rather than being rewritten \u2014 main is pushed and shared, and rewriting it to hide a hole in a history-integrity chain would be its own kind of lie. What is NOT built, and is the real fix: nothing enforces this. The gate catches it *after* the merge, on main, where it is expensive; a pre-merge check that a branch touches docs/design/reflow2.json in at most one commit would catch it while it is still free. That check is cheap (git log --name-only origin/main..HEAD) and belongs in CI on the pull-request trigger. Size S COROLLARY FOUND THE SAME DAY, while building BL-141(b) on a branch stacked on this fix: a STACKED branch inherits its parent PR's exporting commit, so \"one export per PR\" is measured against the main it will actually merge into, not against the branch's own base. Building on an unmerged branch gives you two exporting commits relative to main and the same squash break. The proposed check catches this unchanged \u2014 git log --name-only origin/main..HEAD -- docs/design/reflow2.json | grep -c returns 2, which is exactly the signal \u2014 and that is a point in its favour: it measures the thing that matters rather than the thing that is easy to count. The practical rule: land the parent before stacking, or rebase and re-export once before opening.", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-156 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S."}
